Company description:
Established as a partnership between Cleveland Clinic and Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine (CCLCM) is a unique medical school program that sets standards for the training of physician investigators through innovative approaches to the integration of basic science, research, and clinical medicine.

CCLCM is unique in several ways. Five years are needed to accommodate the research thesis requirement, with many students pursuing an optional master's degree from Case Western Reserve University; the class size each year is limited to 32 students, all of whom receive a full-tuition scholarship; and there are no grades or class rankings throughout the five-year curriculum, with assessment being driven instead by a unique portfolio system.

CCLCM was established in 2002 as a partnership between Cleveland Clinic and Case Western Reserve University with a $100 million gift from Al and Norma Lerner.

Bio:
Dr Tom Wong is consultant cardiologist and electrophysiologist at Royal Brompton & Harefield NHS Foundation Trust. He is also honorary senior lecturer at the National Heart and Lung Institute, Imperial College London.

Areas of expertise
He has a special interest in interventional therapy in the treatment of arrhythmia management including catheter ablation, and device implantation and management. 

Training
He graduated from University of Aberdeen and completed his cardiology training at the Trust.

Dr Wong was awarded a People of the Year award by the Association for Disability and Rehabilitation in 1995 and Young Investigator Award from Heart Rhythm UK in 2005. He was appointed as the clinical director of the cardiac catheterisation laboratories at Royal Brompton Hospital in 2010.

Research
Dr Wong’s research focuses on the interventional treatment of complex cardiac arrhythmia. Specifically in identifying the optimal interventional strategy in treating atrial fibrillation and arrhythmia in patients with heart failure and congenital heart disease.

Publications
Dr Wong has a strong academic record with many publications in international journals such as Circulation, Journal of the American College of Cardiology, European Heart Journal, Circulation Arrhythmia and Electrophysiology, Heart Rhythm Journal, Europace and Journal of Interventional Cardiac Electrophysiology as well as numerous book chapters and articles.

I qualified in medicine with honours from the University of Leicester in 2002. Following basic surgical training in the East Midlands I undertook my doctoral research in the Dept of Transplant Surgery at the University of Leicester under the aegis of Professor Michael Nicholson. Company description:
As the voice of plastic surgery in the UK, we aim to raise awareness of the breadth of plastic surgery, to promote innovation in teaching, learning, and research and to increase overall understanding of the profession. BAPRAS speaks for the majority of reconstructive and aesthetic plastic surgeons providing services to patients in the UK today.

Founded in 1946 in the aftermath of World War 2, as the British Association of Plastic Surgeons, the Association had the objectives of relieving sickness and protecting and preserving public health by the promotion and development of plastic surgery. The aim of the Association was to advance education in all aspects of plastic surgery.

Today, these objectives remain. However, techniques and expertise have progressed to the extent that plastic surgery needs to be understood in a modern, wider context. While the majority of plastic surgery work is reconstructive, restoring form and function following illness or trauma, the world knows that some is aesthetic or ‘cosmetic'​, where people elect for plastic surgery to change form or appearance. As innovative techniques develop, both reconstructive and aesthetic plastic surgery inform each other. The one improves the other, and vice versa, which can only be in the interest of all patients.

As the voice of plastic surgery, BAPRAS sees its role as increasing understanding of the scope of plastic surgery. We aim to raise the profile of plastic surgeons as an intrinsic element of care teams providing specialist care to patients with a wide range of conditions. Continuing our objective of advancing education, BAPRAS is always looking to promote innovation within the speciality of plastic surgery.

Our website bapras.org.uk is a resource for plastic surgeons and other medical professionals.

Bio:
Nima Heidari is an orthopaedic and trauma surgeon renowned for his expertise in bone infection, foot and ankle conditions, including sports injuries, fractures, arthritis, and deformities. In 2012, he was appointed as a consultant at The Royal London Hospital, the UK's largest trauma center, where he set up and led the Bone Infection and Limb Reconstruction services. Under his leadership, the unit expanded into a comprehensive orthoplastic team comprising five consultants, three registrars, one fellow, and support from two allied health professionals. After a dedicated tenure, Professor Heidari has retired from the NHS.

Beyond his clinical practice, he has made significant contributions to medical education and research. He holds an MSc from University College London and a PhD from the George Emil Palade University of Medicine, Pharmacy, Science, and Technology of Targu Mures, where he serves as a Visiting Professor. As the founder of OS Clinic, he has established a leading private orthopaedic practice. Notably, he developed the only orthoplastics and diabetic foot unit in London's private sector at The London Clinic. Professor Heidari has authored over 90 peer-reviewed articles and several book chapters, focusing on precision medicine and the role of AI in healthcare  as well as limb reconstruction techniques, bone biologics, and fracture fixation methods. His commitment to education is further demonstrated through his role as chairman of the UK AO Foot Course for the past eight years and chair of the Advanced Foot Course for AO in Davos.

In addition to his medical achievements, Professor Heidari serves as the Senior Vice President and Chief Medical Officer at European Quantum, a company dedicated to integrating artificial intelligence and machine learning into healthcare. In this role, he explores the application of AI to enhance clinical decision-making and patient outcomes, particularly in joint preservation for arthritis. His work at European Quantum reflects his commitment to the security of personal and sensitive data as well as a sustainable approach to use of AI improve patient care and the preservation of the environment.

Professor Heidari is dedicated to patient care, medical education, and innovative research. His contributions have significantly advanced the field of orthopaedic surgery, particularly in the treatment of osteomyelitis as well as foot and ankle conditions, and his ongoing work continues to shape the future of medical practice.

Bio:
I am a Consultant Vascular and Endovascular Surgeon at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, passionately committed to providing exceptional care since 2013. My surgical journey began in Glasgow in 2001, followed by specialist training in vascular and endovascular surgery at Edinburgh Royal Infirmary in 2008.

My mission is to deliver the best outcomes for my patients, with a focus on treating complex aortic arch, thoracic, and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms. I also excel in minimally invasive treatments for varicose veins, including glue, radiofrequency ablation, and foam sclerotherapy.

As the Lead Clinician of the Scottish National Service for Aortic Arch, Thoracoabdominal, and Suprarenal Aortic Aneurysms, I play a pivotal role in shaping the care and management of patients with these complex conditions. My responsibilities include coordinating a multidisciplinary team of specialists, overseeing clinical protocols, and ensuring that our service remains at the cutting edge of medical advancements. I am dedicated to integrating the latest research and innovative techniques into our treatment plans, continually improving patient outcomes. This leadership position also involves collaborating with healthcare providers across Scotland to standardize care and implement best practices.

In my role as an Honorary Clinical Senior Lecturer at the University of Edinburgh, I stay at the forefront of medical education and innovation, directly benefiting my patients. I also serve as an MRCS Examiner for the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh and an Intercollegiate Specialty Board Examiner in Vascular Surgery (FRCS) and European Board Examiner in Vascular Surgery (FEBVS).

I hold several esteemed professional qualifications, including the Intercollegiate Specialty Board in General Surgery/Vascular Subspecialty FRCS(Ed)(Gen.Vasc) ,Fellow of the American College of Surgeons (FACS),Full Membership MRCS(Ed), Jordanian Board of Vascular Surgery(JBVS), Certificate of Completion of Basic Surgical Training (CCBST),an MBBS from Jordan University of Science and Technology.

Headline: Consultant Hip Orthopaedic Surgeon at Cleveland Clinic London
Bio:
Professor Alister Hart holds the Action Medical Research Chair of Academic Clinical Orthopaedics at University College London (UCL) and is an honorary consultant orthopaedic surgeon at the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital (RNOH) NHS Trust. 

He focusses on hip and knee problems, with an interest in precision placement of implants and understanding why they sometimes function poorly. He was nicknamed the “Hospital Hip Detective” by the BBC. He has done more than 3000 surgical operations including >500 revision hip replacements.

His Impact Case study for the 2014 UCL REF on implant science included: changes to international health policy; development of clinical guidance in the UK and abroad; changes to clinical practice and subsequent cost savings; and accountability within industry.

He has been Principal Investigator on 26 grant awards since 2006 with total funding of over £7 million from research councils, charities and industry. He has published more than 150 papers (first or last author on >100) with 200 co-authors, including in the journal Nature, >4000 citations and an h index of 34. 

He has reviewed for 10 journals. He has given invited lectures in the USA, Canada, Japan, Finland, Italy, Germany, Switzerland, Ireland, and Poland on hip and knee surgery. His medicolegal work has been successfully used by both claimants and defendants.

Bio: I am a Consultant Oesophago-Gastric and Bariatric Surgeon, Clinical Director of Upper GI Surgery and Intestinal Failure at Salford Royal Hospital (NCA Foundation Trust, Manchester), and Honorary Clinical Professor in the Faculty of Biology, Medicine and Health at the University of Manchester.I qualified from the University of Manchester in 2003, completed Higher Surgical Training in the North West of England, and was appointed Consultant Upper Gastrointestinal Surgeon in 2013.My clinical practice centres on complex benign and malignant oesophago-gastric disease and obesity, with a strong focus on minimally invasive and robotic surgery. Headline: Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon
Bio:
Professor Benedict Rogers is a Consultant in Orthopaedic & Trauma Surgery consulting in Surrey and Sussex.

He is an NHS Consultant at Brighton & Sussex University Hospitals NHS Trust and an Honorary  Clinical Professor at Brighton & Sussex Medical School (University of Sussex).

He is the Kent, Surrey & Sussex (KSS) Honorary Academic Lead for Surgery with clinical and academic interests on hip and knee surgery, sports injuries and trauma.

Benedict is a graduate of University of Oxford (Christ Church), St George’s Hospital Medical School (University of London), UCL and University of Toronto.

Benedict was trained in the South West Thames Orthopaedic Programme during which time he was awarded the FRCS (Orth) and subsequent CCT in Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery. His clinical and research interests centre on hip and knee arthroplasty, pelvic and acetabular surgery, lower limb trauma and reconstructive surgery.

Awarded PhD in 2017 with thesis entitled “Optimising the Outcomes of Hip and Knee Replacements”

Benedict undertook two clinical fellowships at Mount Sinai Hospital Hospital & Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre; both world-renowned academic units at University of Toronto
He was trained by several eminent surgeons including Professor Allan Gross, Professor Hans Kreder, Professor Marvin Tile, Dr Joseph Schatzker. 

He was awarded the Zane Cohen Fellowship Achievement Award by the University of Toronto; the first time this had been awarded to an orthopaedic surgeon.

With an extensive and ongoing research portfolio covering basic science and clinical practice, he currently has over 70 publications, over 10 book chapters and over 80 presentations; including several at the British Orthopaedic Association and American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons, with a number awarded prizes. In addition, he has collaborated in studies with various university departments and orthopaedic companies and is a reviewer for the Journal of Bone & Joint Surgery (Br) and JBJS Am.

Bio:
I am a senior consultant in NHS general and specialist surgical practice to the University Hospital in Southampton and to the NHS Treatment Centre at the Royal South Hants Hospital. My independent surgical practice is conducted at the Spire Hospital Southampton.

I am broadly trained in General and Trauma Surgery. However, my current specialist professional focus (2020) is in the management of Breast Disorders, including Breast Cancer; Thyroid and Parathyroid Disorders. 

I also have a medico-legal practice, specialising in advisory reports in civil case law for claimants and defendants on an approximate 50/50 workload split.

In addition to my clinical workload, I play a leading role in the digital innovation programme  at University Hospital Southampton (UHS). In particular, I have conceived and led the UHS Lifelines design, development and implementation programme, since inception in 2009 to full implementation in 2017 across the UHS Clinical Data Estate for all hospital staff and 2.5M clinical records.

UHS Lifelines represents a radical approach to visualisation and interaction with the Electronic Patient Record, through the used of stacked, synchronised and subject specific timelines to display interactive icons, which in turn represent documents, reports, results and events.

This system allows an entire patient record to be displayed and interrogated on a single screen, thus substantially reducing the time to assess and evaluate the case, and the risk of missing critical information.
The agile and iterative processes through which this and our related innovation systems have been built mirror the work and teachings of the UK Government Digital Service. 

Work is continuing to expand its role as a framework application for the  "whole of life" personal electronic health record for all citizens, and we welcome discussions and collaborations will all interested parties.

Bio:
Professor David Ralph is Professor of Urology at UCLH and UCL, London since 1996. He is currently Chairman of The European Society of Genitourethral Reconstructive Surgeons, President of the Sexual Advice Association charity and a specialist advisor to NICE.

He founded the national penile cancer centre at UCLH, the international training centre for penile prostheses insertion and the major phallic reconstruction unit. It is also the biggest priapism centre in the UK.

He has over 250 peer-reviewed publication, 60 chapters and books, 500 international presentations and 500 invited lectures. Company description:
🌟 Reimagining Domiciliary Care: An App to Empower Carers and Elevate Client Wellbeing 🌟

Domiciliary care professionals know all too well the hurdles of supporting individuals in their own homes. From detecting subtle health changes to ensuring consistent training across diverse carer teams, every day presents new complexities. Many agencies struggle with:

⚠️ Early Detection of Decline
Subtle warning signs of conditions like delirium, dehydration, or infection can be missed without a standardised approach.

🎓 Variable Training
With carers coming from different backgrounds, ensuring a uniform skill set can be difficult.

⏰ Lack of Real-Time Support
Working in isolation often means carers must make urgent decisions without immediate backup.

Our Vision: A Groundbreaking Digital Tool
Dr. Kirsten Protherough and Liz Black Lock (founder of Lapis Care) are determined to address these challenges with a purpose-built app, designed by carers for carers. Though we’re still in the development stage, our goal is clear: to create a user-friendly, tech-enabled solution that simplifies day-to-day tasks, strengthens training, and ultimately improves client outcomes.

Key Features on Our Drawing Board
✅ Streamlined Assessment
A digital checklist and prompt system to help carers quickly spot early warning signs of deterioration.

📚 Interactive Training Modules
Engaging video lessons, quizzes, and case studies to build confidence and maintain consistent standards.

💬 Real-Time Expert Support
A built-in messaging feature to connect carers with supervisors or specialists whenever they need guidance.

📊 Comprehensive Reporting
Easy-to-generate summaries for auditing, quality checks, and updates to family members or healthcare teams.

Why Now?
📈 Growing Demand
As more people choose to remain in their homes, the need for innovative tools that support domiciliary care is greater than ever.

❤️ Better Outcomes
Early detection and standardised training

Bio:
Mr. Jonathan J.R. Richardson is an experienced Colorectal and General Surgeon practising in the West Midlands of England.

Mr. Richardson was appointed as a Consultant Colorectal and General Surgeon at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust, in 2017.  

Mr. Richardson has clinical interests across the full range of colorectal and general surgery. He has a major interest in the management of colorectal cancer and the use of laparoscopic (and now robotic) surgical techniques. He is a high volume colorectal cancer resection surgeon with excellent patient outcomes. He also undertakes complex surgery for the management of locally advanced colorectal cancer.  Mr. Richardson is a core member of the Colorectal Cancer Multi-disciplinary Team and is the Clinical Lead for Enhanced Recovery After Surgery.  Mr. Richardson holds the management position of Governance Lead for the Surgical Directorate and strives to attain optimal patient outcomes and safety.

Mr. Richardson has undertaken a period of research and he was the Chief Investigator of a translational research study which successfully characterised systemic neutrophil function in patients undergoing colorectal cancer resection.  He presented the results of his research internationally and was awarded the prestigious European Society for Surgical Research Best Clinical Research Award.  He was awarded an MD from the University of Birmingham for his thesis submission and his research has been published in peer reviewed medical journals.

Mr. Richardson is heavily involved in clinical research.  He is the Principal Investigator and Co-investigator of multiple NIHR portfolio studies and is consistently one of the highest recruiters to clinical trials at University Hospitals Birmingham.  In addition, Mr. Richardson has published and presented widely on a variety of colorectal and general surgical conditions contributing to the surgical academic literature. 

Mr. Richardson has an extensive experience in organising and delivering teaching.  During surgical training he formalised his teaching skills and he was awarded a Postgraduate Certificate in Medical Education.  In his current Consultant position, Mr. Richardson is the Lead Undergraduate Surgical Tutor and a Senior Clinical Examiner at the University of Birmingham and he has been appointed as an Honorary Associate Professor at the University of Birmingham.  Mr. Richardson is a GMC accredited Named Educational Supervisor and the Faculty Lead for the Royal College of Surgeons Basic Surgical Skills course.

Prof Bijayendra Singh is one of the leading Upper Limb Surgeons in Kent and South East of England. He is fondly known as Bijay or BJ
I began my medical career earning my degree from Maharaja Sayajirao University in Vadodara, India, where I first developed an interest in upper limb orthopaedics through my thesis on Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
I pursued advanced training in the UK and completed prestigious fellowships at globally renowned institutions, including:
•	Perth Orthopaedics & Sports Medicine Centre (Australia)
•	Kleinert & Kutz Hand Institute (USA)

What I Do
Performing over 800 procedures annually, I specialize in both routine and complex cases. My expertise includes:
•	Shoulder: Rotator cuff tears, impingement, arthritis, frozen shoulder, and dislocations.
•	Elbow: Tennis elbow, Golfer’s elbow, Elbow Arthritis, and Trapped Nerve.
•	Wrist & Hand: Carpal tunnel syndrome, Finger and Wrist arthritis, Trigger Finger, Ganglion cysts, and Dupuytren’s contracture.
•	Trauma: Complex upper limb fractures requiring advanced surgical management.
With a commitment to shared decision-making, I ensure each patient receives a tailored treatment plan that aligns with their needs and goals.
 
Teaching & Research
Education and research are integral to my practice. As a Visiting Professor at Canterbury Christchurch University and the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, I am dedicated to mentoring the next generation of surgeons.
•	Over 100 publications in national and international journals.
•	120+ presentations at leading medical conferences.
•	Faculty member of the F.R.C.S. (Orth) Course and examiner at GKT Medical School.
Whether through lectures, hands-on training, or mentorship, I am passionate about advancing the field of upper limb orthopaedics. I enjoy engaging with medical students, trainees, and even aspiring medics in secondary schools, offering insights into a career in medicine and guidance through mock interviews as well promoting work experience for sixth form students.
 
Beyond Medicine
Outside of the operating theatre, I enjoy spending time with my wife, a GP, and our two daughters. I am passionate about cooking (especially perfecting my Butter Chicken recipe), cycling, and gardening. At home, our lively discussions keep us engaged and often inspire new perspectives.

Company description:
Robotic Surgery Healthcare (RoSH) is an independent, clinically led initiative supporting the safe, effective and sustainable development of robotic-assisted surgery.

Our mission is to help more people access the benefits of robotic-assisted surgery where supported by evidence and appropriate to clinical need.

We view robotic surgery not simply as a technology, but as a healthcare-delivery system. Its success depends on clinical evidence, trained multidisciplinary teams, robust governance, safe theatre integration, efficient pathways and sustainable value.

Our work focuses on:
• Robotic programme design, adoption and optimisation
• Theatre integration, workflow and operational efficiency
• Workforce capability, education and multidisciplinary practice
• Patient safety, clinical governance and emergency readiness
• Equitable access, interoperability and sustainable value
• Collaboration across clinical practice, policy, research and responsible industry

RoSH is clinically led, platform-neutral and multidisciplinary. We welcome dialogue and collaboration with healthcare providers, clinicians, professional bodies, policymakers, researchers, patient representatives and industry partners who share our commitment to responsible robotic surgery development.

Founded by Carmine Civilli BSc (Hons), MSc, Surgical Care Practitioner and robotic surgery clinical operations specialist.

Bio: Emma Stapleton is a Consultant Otolaryngologist (ENT Surgeon), Otologist, and Auditory Implant Surgeon in Manchester, UK, specialising in cochlear implantation, complex ear surgery, hearing loss, and dizziness/balance. She is Clinical Lead for the Manchester Auditory Implant Programmes since 2021, practising across NHS and private care, and maintains a high-volume subspecialty practice performing over 100 auditory implant procedures annually.Her clinical and research expertise encompasses cochlear implants, local anaesthetic cochlear implantation, hearing preservation, robotic and technology-assisted implant surgery, middle ear implants, bone-conduction hearing devices, otosclerosis, stapes surgery, ossiculoplasty, tympanoplasty, and complex ear disease. She has particular subspecialty expertise in necrotising otitis externa (NOE) and is currently undertaking a PhD at the University of Manchester investigating the impact of Type 2 diabetes on audiovestibular function.In 2025, she performed the UK’s first robot-assisted cochlear implantations. Internationally recognised for her surgical innovation, she has delivered more than 150 invited lectures across 18 countries, including as Guest of Honour at the American Otological Society 2024.Stapleton holds the highest level National Clinical Impact Award, and received the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh (RCSEd) Hunter–Doig Medal in 2022. She is an elected member of RCSEd Council, leads its National Surgical and Dental Mentoring Programme, and is Editor of Surgeons’ News magazine. She is a former Chair of Women in ENT UK (WENTS) and Past President of the North of England Otolaryngology Society.She serves as Honorary Secretary of the British Cochlear Implant Group (BCIG), a Trustee of the TWJ Foundation, and a Trustee and Director of the Journal of Laryngology & Otology, where she also serves as an Associate Editor. She is regularly invited to advise NICE and national healthcare policy bodies.Alongside clinical practice, Stapleton leads clinical, translational, and health services research in hearing science and auditory implantation. She serves as Chief Investigator for the DETECT study and Principal Investigator for multicentre trials including the COACH study. The author of over 60 peer-reviewed publications and multiple international textbook chapters, she actively supervises medical students, MSc candidates, and surgical trainees in collaboration with the University of Manchester.

Company description:
This is the official LinkedIn page for the HM Courts & Tribunals Service.  Find all our channels: https://linktr.ee/HMCTSofficial 

We are responsible for the administration of criminal, civil and family courts and tribunals in England and Wales.

We are also responsible for non-devolved tribunals in Scotland and Northern Ireland. We work with an independent judiciary to provide a fair, efficient and effective justice system.

We employ around 17,000 staff and operate from locations in England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

Through the courts and tribunals we give people and businesses access to justice, including:

- victims and witnesses of crime
- defendants accused of crimes
- consumers in debt or with other disputes
- people involved in the adoption or protection of children
- businesses involved in commercial disputes
- individuals asserting their employment rights or challenging the decisions of government bodies
- people affected by relationship breakdown

We follow the Ministry of Justice’s strategic vision for reform, to create a more effective, less costly and more responsive justice system for the public.

We’re responsible for:
- providing the supporting administration for a fair, efficient and accessible courts and tribunal system
- supporting an independent judiciary in the administration of justice
- driving improvements across all aspects of the administration of the courts and tribunals
- collaborating effectively with other justice organisations and agencies, including the legal professions, to improve   
  access to justice
- working with government departments and agencies to improve the quality and timeliness of their decision- 
  making, which will reduce the number of cases coming before courts and tribunals
